biography: Dries Vanthoor, the 'Vegas Flash,' hails from Hasselt, Belgium, a town more known for its jenever than its jump starts. From the age of seven, karting was his obsession, fueled by his father's tales of rallying glory. He wasn’t just participating; he was dominating, earning the nickname 'Pocket Rocket' for his aggressive, all-or-nothing style, even back then. A pivotal moment came during a junior karting championship race when, despite starting last due to a mechanical issue, he clawed his way to the front, executing a daring last-corner overtake that cemented his reputation for audacious maneuvers. After winning the European Le Mans series, his career stalled due to lack of budget, but his undeniable talent landed him a spot with the Vegas Yellow Matte team, where he's been steadily climbing the ranks, proving that flashy isn’t just for paint jobs.
drivingStyle: Vanthoor's driving is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He's known for his late-braking overtakes and willingness to push the car to its absolute limit, often flirting with the edge of grip. Tire management is a work in progress; he tends to overdrive early in a stint, sacrificing longevity for immediate pace. Under pressure, he either thrives, pulling off miraculous performances, or cracks, making uncharacteristic errors. His mantra is simple: flat out or nothing.

rivalries.reason: A clash of egos and driving styles. Rossi, known for his calculated precision, openly criticizes Vanthoor's 'reckless' approach, leading to heated exchanges both on and off the track.
A fierce on-track battle for championship points in the GT series resulted in several close calls and accusations of blocking, sparking a rivalry that continues to simmer.
Their shared ambition to win the 24 Hours of Le Mans has led to intense competition, with both drivers constantly trying to outdo each other in terms of lap times and race strategies.

quirks: Always wears the same lucky pair of 'Vegas Yellow' socks for every race.
Refuses to look at the starting grid until five minutes before the race begins, claiming it 'jinxes' his performance.
Listens to a specific obscure Belgian techno track on repeat during the formation lap.
famousQuote: Second place is just the first loser.
careerHighlight: Winning the European Le Mans Series at the age of 20, proving his talent on a global stage and securing his place in the world of professional racing.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final hour of the Spa 24 Hours in 2022, costing his team a potential victory on home soil.
